Every glyph in `GLYPHS` is exactly 5 chars wide, so all 5 rows of "LUNA" are naturally the same length (24 chars) — until `.replace(/\s+$/, '')` strips a *different* amount of trailing space off each row (because the last letter, `A`, has different trailing-space patterns per row: `' ███ '` vs `'█   █'`). That made row 0 of LUNA 22 chars and row 4 of LUNA 23 chars. Since `artRows()` then appends CORE right after LUNA with a fixed 2-space gap, CORE's starting column shifted by a character between rows — so each row of the magenta "CORE" glyphs landed one column off from the row above/below it, shearing the letters into that overlapping, broken look. It's the terminal-text equivalent of two misaligned columns, exactly what you're seeing.

**Fix:** stop trimming LUNA per-row (keep it at its natural uniform width so CORE always starts at the same column on every row):
